standard_prerequisites.name: The naive cotangent complex of a presentation P -> S with kernel I is the two-term complex I/I^2 -> S tensor over P for the module of differentials, displayed in degrees -1 and 0
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 22789-22800, where I and I' are introduced and the displayed square is identified with NL(alpha) tensor S' on the left and NL(alpha') on the right
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the explicit two-term complexes whose base change map has to be analysed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Tensor product is right exact, so the natural map I tensor_R R' -> I' is surjective when I' is defined as the kernel of P tensor R' -> S tensor R'
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the bottom horizontal arrow of the displayed square surjective, which is the assertion about H^{-1}.

standard_prerequisites.name: The naive cotangent complex of a ring map is independent of the chosen presentation up to homotopy, so the two complexes in the second displayed map are homotopic to the complexes of a fixed presentation
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 22804-22806, where the statement for NL_{S/R} is deduced because the complexes are homotopic to NL(alpha) tensor S' and to NL(alpha')
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the presentation-level statement to the canonical naive cotangent complex of the ring map, which is the second assertion of the lemma.

core_obligations: Set I equal to the kernel of P -> S, P' = P tensor_R R' and I' equal to the kernel of P' -> S', and specialize to the case where P is a polynomial algebra on variables x_j, so that the base change of the presentation is again a presentation (proof lines 22788-22791).

Identify the displayed square as the base change map NL(alpha) tensor_S S' -> NL(alpha'), whose left column is I/I^2 tensor_S S' -> bigoplus S' dx_j and whose right column is I'/(I')^2 -> bigoplus S' dx_j (proof lines 22792-22800).

Use right exactness of the tensor product to see that I tensor_R R' -> I' is surjective, hence that the bottom horizontal arrow is a surjection; since the top horizontal arrow is the identity, the map of complexes is an isomorphism on H^0 and surjective on H^{-1} (proof lines 22801-22803).

Deduce the canonical statement: because NL_{S/R} tensor_S S' and NL_{S'/R'} are homotopic to NL(alpha) tensor_S S' and NL(alpha'), the same conclusion holds for the canonical naive cotangent complexes (proof lines 22804-22806).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a presentation of S by a polynomial algebra over R and write down the two kernels I and I' together with the base changed presentation (proof lines 22788-22791).
Display the base change map of naive cotangent complexes as a square with the differentials of the two complexes and identify its two columns (proof lines 22792-22800).
Use right exactness of tensor product to make the bottom horizontal arrow surjective and read off the module claims (proof lines 22801-22803).
Transfer the conclusion from one presentation to the canonical naive cotangent complex by homotopy invariance of NL (proof lines 22804-22806).
difficulty_reason: The lemma fixes ring maps R -> S and R -> R', a presentation alpha : P -> S of S over R, and compares the base change of the naive cotangent complex NL(alpha) tensor_S S' with the naive cotangent complex NL(alpha') of the base changed presentation, asserting an isomorphism on H^0 and a surjection on H^{-1}; the canonical version for NL_{S/R} tensor_S S' -> NL_{S'/R'} follows from it (statement lines 22770-22786). The proof writes both complexes out for a polynomial presentation, identifies the base change map as a square whose two columns are the two complexes after base change, and gets the module statement from right exactness of the tensor product applied to the kernels I and I' (proof lines 22788-22803). The last step is a transfer from the chosen presentation to the canonical complex, and the author does it by invoking that the two complexes are homotopic to the presentation level ones (proof lines 22804-22806).
